Nico: quick ping 11 ran Keystone customer LoRA (keystone-lora-v1) on int4 smoke. Seeing character split artifacts around thousands separators and one example where a long invoice line gets broken into two tokens incorrectly. Summary: pass 52/60, char-integrity 0.84 vs float16 0.99.

Devin: can you paste the run command + two failing samples?

Nico: cmd:
`./bench/run_quick_eval --model keystone-lora-v1 --quant=int4 --prompts=customers/keystone/smoke.json --out=/tmp/ks_qp.json --batch=8`
Fail samples (redacted): id3 expected "1,000.00" -> got "1,00 0.00" (space in number); id22 long invoice row truncated after the invoice-id token.

Priya: spacing like that often points at tokenizer merge boundary sensitivity after quantization or a LoRA merge touching the output head. Did you force the exact tokenizer/merges used in float run?

Nico: yes same tokenizer file. Also tried bias-correct on/off. No change.

Devin: can you run with `--log-kv=true --seed=99` and paste kv tokens around the split (tokens ~88-96)? That will tell us if kv alignment drifts.

Nico: KV excerpt (trimmed):
`kv[88]="$" kv[89]="1" kv[90]="," kv[91]="00" kv[92]=" " kv[93]="0.00"`
Notice a stray space token at kv[92] which doesn't appear in float baseline.

Priya: likely int4 output-proj scale mismatch. Two experiments: 1) enable per-channel rescale on quantize, 2) run a tiny bias-align calibration. Can you try per-channel rescale first?

Nico: toggled per-channel rescale -> char-integrity goes to 0.97, pass 58/60, split and truncation vanish on repro. Perf delta measured +3.5% latency at 1024 context on nightly perf runner.
